output.title: Sliced bread loaf packing (cool, slice, bag, label, crate)

product.name: Bagged sliced sandwich loaf
product.description: A baked sandwich loaf is sliced, placed into a plastic bag, closed with a clip, and date-labelled. Unit size about 280 × 110 × 120 mm (0.28 × 0.11 × 0.12 m).

steps.name: CoolLoaves
steps.does: Loaves cool after coming from the oven while moving through the line before slicing.

steps.name: SliceLoaves
steps.does: Slice each loaf into sandwich slices.

steps.name: BagLoaves
steps.does: Place the sliced loaf into a plastic bag.

steps.name: ClipBag
steps.does: Close the plastic bag using a clip.

steps.name: ApplyDateLabel
steps.does: Apply a date label onto the closed bag.

steps.name: WeighCheck
steps.does: Weigh each bag using a check weigher and decide PASS/REJECT based on minimum weight.

steps.name: CratePackedLoaves
steps.does: Place accepted (packed) loaves into crates for shipment.

output.quality: Lightweight loaves are rejected by the check weigher (typically diverted to a reject chute/bin for later handling/repaste or disposal).
constraints: Food-grade, high hygiene throughout (sanitation and hygienic machine design).
Loaves are cooled between oven exit and slicing.
assumptions: Owner’s stated 1200 loaves/hour is the finished unit rate (one date-labelled, bagged loaf per unit).
If no shift length was provided, the line rate is interpreted for an 8-hour shift (takt computed from per-hour rate).
Reject handling for light loaves is a diversion to a dedicated reject bin/chute; no rework is specified.
Cooling is accomplished by controlled transport time/accumulation on the line (not a separate long blast tunnel).

questions.question: Confirm what counts as the finished unit: one bagged + clipped + date-labelled sliced loaf, or the entire crate? (I assumed per loaf bag.)
questions.why: This determines the unit definition for throughput and station takt.

questions.question: How are loaves presented between steps: individual loaves in single file, or in small batches/throughput carriers from the oven/slicer?
questions.why: It decides conveyor type (belt vs indexed carriers) and how to stage cooling/slicing without bottlenecks.

questions.question: What are the target rejection/accept criteria and flow style for the check weigher (e.g., divert method, reject pocket size, acceptable weight band)?
questions.why: It affects the weigher decision timing and whether the reject divert station fits within the takt at 1200/hr.
